sections.title: Letter dê
paragraphs: The letter (dê) /de/ makes the sound /d/. You can hear it in (dia) /ˈdi.ɐ/, which means day. This letter has only one sound in European Portuguese.

sections.title: Making the sound
paragraphs: Press the tip of your tongue against the back of your top teeth. Build up a little air behind your tongue. Release the air suddenly while you make a sound with your voice. You can feel your vocal cords vibrate if you touch your throat.

sections.title: Reading this letter
paragraphs: This letter always makes the sound /d/. It keeps this sound at the beginning of a word and after vowels or consonants. For example, it sounds like this in (onde) /ˈõ.dɨ/.

sections.title: Avoiding mistakes
paragraphs: In English, you often touch the gum ridge behind your teeth to say door. In Portuguese, touch the back of your upper teeth instead. Keep your tongue further forward to avoid a heavy English sound.
